title: Tail-aware dual-rate autoscaler + tenant throughput bounder
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see tenant-driven microbursts and long-tail latency spikes that cause oscillation in the current single-window autoscaler. Some tenants sustain high qps while others produce short, intense bursts; the existing policy either over-provisions for bursts (wasting dedicated capacity) or under-reacts to tail-latency regressions (breaking SLAs).

This PR introduces two coordinated runtime controls: (1) a tail-aware dual-rate autoscaler that reasons over a fast (burst) window and a slow (sustained) window and applies a penalizer based on observed tail latency; and (2) a tenant throughput bounder that enforces soft tenant-level throughput caps with graceful degradation paths to isolate noisy tenants. Together these controls aim to reduce thrash, keep p99/p999 SLOs stable, and limit cross-tenant interference while preserving overall fleet utilization.

What changed (summary):
- Add pkg/autoscaler/dual_rate_autoscaler.go: new controller that maintains two exponentially-weighted windows (burstWindow=30s, sustainedWindow=10m) and a latency penalizer computed from tenant p99/p999. The controller outputs a targetConcurrency per-tenant with min/max guards and hysteresis.
- Add pkg/autoscaler/throughput_bounder.go: an admission shim applied at the fleet gate that tracks tenant token buckets (soft tokens) and emits fallback decisions (defer, throttle, fallback-model).
- Telemetry: introduce metrics redwood_autoscaler_dual_rate_target, redwood_autoscaler_tail_penalty, redwood_bounder_tokens{tenant}, redwood_bounder_actions_total. Instrumentation added to observability-pack dashboards and perf-canary scenarios.
- Config: new api types in api/v1alpha/autoscaler_config.proto and defaults in config/defaults.yaml.
- CLI/UX: add fleetctl quota debug command (cmd/fleetctl/quota_debug.go) to inspect tenant tokens and recent decisions.
- Tests: unit tests for both controllers, integration test that runs a synthetic burst scenario against a small local cluster, and a lightweight e2e harness for canary.
- Docs: update redwood-docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md with algorithm notes, config knobs, and rollout guidance.

Behavioral notes: The dual-rate autoscaler multiplies the sustained target by a burst multiplier when burstWindow utilization consistently exceeds burstThreshold AND the latency penalizer is low. If tail latency rises above penalizeThreshold, the penalizer reduces effective burst multiplier and triggers backlog-level preemption for non-critical tenants in the bounder. The throughput bounder is soft by default: it recommends actions (log/metrics), then can be toggled to actively throttle specific tenants.

Testing & verification:
- Unit: autoscaler window math, hysteresis, penalizer thresholds, bounder token accounting.
- Integration: simulated tenants A/B with different arrival patterns (steady high qps vs short bursts). Verified reduced oscillation, ~18% lower peak spare capacity (compared to current headroom strategy) and ~22% fewer latency-SLO violations in bursty tests.
- Canary: rolled to two warm pools (canary-1, canary-2) for 72h. Observed stable p99 and reduced churn in pod allocations.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged default-off. Deploy mainline with flags in defaults.yaml.
2) Enable read-only telemetry in prod to collect baseline metrics for 24-48h.
3) Toggle soft-bounder (reporting only) for a subset of fleets and run canary harness.
4) Enable active bounder for low-risk tenants; expand if metrics look stable.
5) Enable full dual-rate autoscaler in dedicated fleets with gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor cost & latency dashboards.

Operational guidance:
- Key metrics to watch: redwood_autoscaler_tail_penalty (goal: <0.2), redwood_bounder_actions_total (expect occasional throttle events), per-tenant p99/p999 and utilization.
- If tenants see throttling: use fleetctl quota_debug to inspect tokens and adjust tenant soft_quota in the config or mark tenant as critical to opt out of bounder.

Backward compatibility & migration: non-breaking by default (feature gated). No schema changes to tenant objects. New config fields have safe defaults.

Related work: builds on ENG-3182 (per-tenant eviction thresholds) and SRE-56 (headroom smoothing). Follow-up tasks: tune default thresholds based on wider fleet telemetry (ENG-4312).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration + canary harness
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Telemetry dashboards updated
- [x] Rollout playbook included

review_comments: Elliot Park: Can you justify the chosen burstWindow=30s vs 60s? In some clusters bursts are very short. Also request a brief explanation on interaction with prefix caching.

Ava Chen: Chose 30s after perf bench showing faster decay reduces unnecessary warm pool spin-ups for 90% of tenants. Added comment in code and extended integration tests to cover 15s/30s/60s. The autoscaler is orthogonal to prefix caching — caching reduces per-token cost but this control focuses on allocation rhythm.
Maya Singh: Add a safety cutoff if penalizer flips frequently causing oscillation. Suggest a minimum cooloff=120s between scale-downs.
Ava Chen: Added downCooldown=120s and unit tests. Also added metrics to track cooldown events.
Tariq Al-Masri: Bounder action list should include a 'fallback-model' decision. Also asked for a short playbook for tenant ops.
Ava Chen: Added fallback-model action and appended a tenant ops section in docs with 'how to debug' and recommended knobs.
release_notes: (dedicated) Introduces a dual-rate autoscaler (burst+sustained windows) and an optional tenant throughput bounder to stabilize allocations and limit noisy-tenant impact. Feature-flagged and off by default. See docs for rollout steps and tuning guidance.
